main.title: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time
main.subtitle: Two partners on separate journeys
main.summary: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, released in North America on 27 October 2009. Ratchet searches for Clank while learning more about the Lombaxes, and Clank discovers his connection to the Great Clock. Their separation gives each character a different kind of adventure. Ratchet explores planets with an expanding arsenal; Clank solves problems whose main material is time. The story brings together mysteries introduced earlier in the Future saga while keeping the partnership at the centre of its conclusion.

cards.heading: Two partners on separate journeys
cards.text: Ratchet & Clank Future: A Crack in Time is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 platform shooter, released in North America on 27 October 2009. Ratchet searches for Clank while learning more about the Lombaxes, and Clank discovers his connection to the Great Clock. Their separation gives each character a different kind of adventure. Ratchet explores planets with an expanding arsenal; Clank solves problems whose main material is time. The story brings together mysteries introduced earlier in the Future saga while keeping the partnership at the centre of its conclusion.

cards.heading: Record a helper, then become another one
cards.text: Clank can record his actions on special time pads and leave a holographic copy to replay them. The player then performs another part of the task while the recorded Clank repeats its route. Several recordings can work together, holding switches or opening paths in an ordered sequence. Solving a room involves planning what each version must do and when the next action becomes possible. The puzzle turns a single controlled character into a small coordinated team whose other members are the player's own previous decisions.

cards.heading: Room to travel between the planets
cards.text: Ratchet gains hoverboots that carry him quickly across surfaces and launch him over gaps. Space travel also provides small moons and optional activities between the major destinations, giving the search a less direct route. Weapons retain the series' comic effects and improve through use, while Clank's staff repairs damaged objects inside the Clock. Brian Allgeier directed, with Boris Salchow composing the score. Critics praised the combination of story and play. The adventure became a major conclusion to the Future storyline before Into the Nexus supplied a later epilogue.

main.title: League of Legends
main.summary: League of Legends (LoL), commonly referred to as League, is a multiplayer online battle arena video game developed and published by Riot Games.

cards.text: League of Legends (LoL), commonly referred to as League, is a multiplayer online battle arena video game developed and published by Riot Games. Inspired by Defense of the Ancients, a custom map for Warcraft III, Riot's founders sought to develop a stand-alone game in the same genre. Since its release in October 2009, League has been free-to-play and is monetized through purchasable character customization. The game is available for Windows and macOS.

In the game's main mode, Summoner's Rift, two teams of five players battle in player-versus-player combat. Each player controls a character, known as a "champion", with unique abilities and styles of play. During a match, champions become more powerful by collecting experience points, earning gold, and purchasing items to defeat the opposing team. Teams defend their base and win by pushing toward the enemy base and destroying a large structure within it, the "Nexus".

League of Legends has received generally favorable reviews, which have highlighted its accessibility, character designs, and production value. The game's long lifespan has resulted in a critical reappraisal, with reviews trending favorably; it is widely considered one of the greatest video games ever made. However, rude and abusive in-game player behavior, criticized since the game's early days, persists despite Riot's attempts to fix the problem. In 2019, League regularly peaked at eight million concurrent players, and its popularity has led to tie-ins such as music, comic books, short stories, and the animated series Arcane. Its success has spawned several spin-off video games, including a mobile version, a digital collectible card game, a trading card game, and a turn-based role-playing game, among others. An MMORPG based on the property is in development.

League of Legends is the world's largest esport, with an international competitive scene consisting of multiple regional leagues which culminates in an annual League of Legends World Championship. The 2019 event registered over 100 million unique viewers, peaking at a concurrent viewership of 44 million during the finals. Domestic and international events have been broadcast on livestreaming websites such as Twitch, YouTube, Bilibili, and the cable television sports channel ESPN.

main.title: LocoRoco Midnight Carnival
main.subtitle: Keep the bounce going after dark
main.summary: A downloadable PSP spin-off builds its challenge around the enhanced Boing bounce, shared stages and a mischievous midnight playground.

cards.heading: The BuiBui interrupt a peaceful night
cards.text: LocoRoco Midnight Carnival arrived on PlayStation Network for PSP on 29 October 2009. This spin-off follows LocoRoco 2 and takes the creatures into a secret playground built by the mischievous BuiBui. Their sleep is interrupted by a trap that sends them into the carnival, where the goal is to overcome its obstacles and return to bed.

cards.heading: Boing turns walls into a route forward
cards.text: The central addition is Boing, a much stronger bounce that sends a LocoRoco off walls and through the stages. Keeping the rebounds going becomes a way to reach the goal and build a higher score. The original release contains sixteen standard stages, two minigames and three bonus stages. It keeps the series’ colourful, rounded shapes while placing greater emphasis on continuous movement and tricky routes.

cards.heading: Dress up and bounce together
cards.text: Up to four players can join stages through local ad hoc play, either cooperating or competing. Accessories bought with collected Pickories can change the creatures’ abilities: the Helper’s Mask, for example, lets a friend carry another player through a difficult section. Global leaderboards add a separate online challenge, and the leading players can share replays for others to watch and learn from.

main.title: Sin and Punishment: Star Successor
main.subtitle: A moving target
main.summary: Sin and Punishment: Star Successor is Treasure’s Wii sequel to the Nintendo 64 shooter. Known in Europe as Successor of the Skies, it follows Isa and Kachi through a succession of tightly staged battles. The route advances automatically, leaving the player to concentrate on aiming, movement and survival within the scene. Wii controls allow the firing direction to be handled independently from the character’s position. That separation gives the screen two simultaneous problems: where to move and where to keep the next attack focused.

cards.heading: A moving target
cards.text: Sin and Punishment: Star Successor is Treasure’s Wii sequel to the Nintendo 64 shooter. Known in Europe as Successor of the Skies, it follows Isa and Kachi through a succession of tightly staged battles. The route advances automatically, leaving the player to concentrate on aiming, movement and survival within the scene. Wii controls allow the firing direction to be handled independently from the character’s position. That separation gives the screen two simultaneous problems: where to move and where to keep the next attack focused.

cards.heading: Space to dodge
cards.text: A rail shooter can appear to restrict movement, yet its pressure comes from the decisions available inside that frame. Enemy fire, targets and obstacles compete for attention while the route keeps changing. Moving safely does not automatically produce a good shot, and following a target can make an approaching threat easier to miss. Star Successor builds on that tension, asking the player to read a scene as it unfolds. The spectacle remains tied to a practical task: making room to survive while continuing to attack.

cards.heading: Turn an attack around
cards.text: A sword strike gives the player an answer to some attacks that a gun cannot provide. At close range it deals heavy damage, and certain incoming projectiles can be struck back toward an opponent. A charge attack offers another burst of power, followed by a longer wait before it can be used again. Successive hits without taking damage build a score multiplier, while reflecting missiles can raise it too. Scoring well therefore rewards reading an attack closely enough to turn it into an advantage.

main.title: Bayonetta
main.summary: Bayonetta turns a last-second dodge into an opening for attack. PlatinumGames’ 2009 action game connects Witch Time, flowing combos and Mari Shimazaki’s character design in a precise combat system.

cards.heading: Bayonetta arrives
cards.text: PlatinumGames developed Bayonetta, published by Sega for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in Japan in October 2009 and internationally in January 2010. The witch fights with guns in her hands and heels, using magically transforming hair as a weapon. Later editions brought the original game to additional consoles and PC.

cards.heading: The first game and its later editions
cards.text: The first game in the series was directed by Hideki Kamiya, who created the Devil May Cry and was involved with the Ōkami franchise while he was working with Capcom. It was the third title in Platinum's four-game contract with Sega. The game was released on October 29, 2009, in Japan, and was released worldwide in January 2010 for Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3. The game received generally positive reviews upon release. More than 1.35 million units of the game were shipped. Although it was Platinum's most commercially successful game at that time, the company was disappointed with its sales. A 4K remastered version of the game featuring anti-aliasing, anisotropic filtering, SSAO lighting, scalable texture and shadow quality, and more was released on PC in April 2017. The game was ported to Nintendo Switch in 2018, and was bundled alongside Vanquish for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in February 2020.

cards.heading: Nintendo supports Bayonetta 2
cards.text: Bayonetta 2 was announced in 2012 during a Nintendo Direct for the Wii U. The decision received backlash from fans, since the game would not be available on other platforms. Platinum was initially working with Sega to create the sequel, but Sega decided to cancel the game during the game's development. Nintendo subsequently revived the project. According to producer Atsushi Inaba, the game would not have been possible if they did not get the funding and the support from Nintendo. Sega remained as the game's consultant. The game was directed by Yusuke Hashimoto, and Kamiya has a supervision role. The game was released in 2014 to very positive reviews. While sales for the Wii U version have not been fully disclosed, by March 2018, Nintendo confirmed the Switch version had sold 400,000 copies during its first nine weeks, compared to the 300,000 copies the Wii U version sold during the same period. As of December 2021, the Switch version has sold 1.04 million copies worldwide.

cards.heading: The third adventure
cards.text: A third game in the series was announced by Nintendo at The Game Awards 2017. A gameplay trailer was shown at the September Nintendo Direct 2021. It was released for the Nintendo Switch on October 28, 2022, and opened with positive reviews from both critics and fans. The game went on to win Best Action Game at the Game Awards 2022. The game also features a playable teaser for Cereza and the Lost Demon as a secret level and unlocks a special skin once found.

cards.heading: Cereza and the Lost Demon
cards.text: A prequel companion game to Bayonetta 3, focusing on Cereza as a young girl, was announced by Nintendo at The Game Awards 2022. It was released on Nintendo Switch on March 17, 2023.

cards.heading: 8-Bit Bayonetta
cards.text: An action/shooter 16-bit-style browser minigame called "8-Bit Bayonetta" was released on February 16, 2015, and later on Steam on March 31, 2017.

cards.heading: Guest appearances
cards.text: Outside of the Bayonetta series, Bayonetta characters have made guest appearances in other Sega and PlatinumGames releases. Bayonetta appears as a downloadable character in the multiplayer fighting game Anarchy Reigns. She, Jeanne, and Rodin also appear a special guest characters in the action game The Wonderful 101. Bayonetta was added as a downloadable character to Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and Wii U, later returning as an unlockable character in the sequel Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. Both games also feature a stage based on the falling Umbra Clock Tower which appeared in the first two Bayonetta games. Rodin also appears as an Assist Trophy in Ultimate. Bayonetta will be added to Sonic Racing CrossWorlds as a playable character via a forthcoming free update.

cards.heading: Four guns in motion
cards.text: Bayonetta's four guns, quick movement and elaborate attacks give its battles a distinctive pace. Combos can continue through a dodge, letting players avoid a blow without giving up their attack. The stages provide room for those movements, with animation and visual effects supporting the heroine's flamboyant fighting style.

cards.heading: Dodging into Witch Time
cards.text: A dodge at the last instant activates Witch Time, slowing enemies and opening an opportunity to attack. Keeping a combo going requires attention to distance, animations and timing. Guns on the hands and heels allow attacks to flow through different poses, while dodging helps maintain the sequence under pressure.

cards.heading: Mari Shimazaki designs a modern witch
cards.text: Mari Shimazaki's initial brief called for a female lead, a modern witch and four guns. The final design took about a year, settling on black as the main colour and glasses as a defining feature. The guns on Bayonetta's heels influenced her poses and silhouette, which had to remain recognisable during fast attacks.

cards.heading: Making room for Bayonetta
cards.text: Early environments proved too small for Bayonetta's movement. Vigrid Station grew by fifty percent to accommodate her range and allow more distance for loading. The team also reduced ideas that slowed the action: using Witch Walk in many areas would have shifted too much attention towards puzzles. The finished spaces were revised around the heroine's speed.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2009
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2009 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Dragon Age: Origins
main.summary: Dragon Age: Origins is a 2009 role-playing video game developed by Canadian studio BioWare and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: The Grey Wardens of Ferelden
cards.text: Dragon Age: Origins is a 2009 role-playing video game developed by Canadian studio BioWare and published by Electronic Arts. It is the first game in the Dragon Age franchise. Set in the fictional kingdom of Ferelden during a period of civil strife, the game puts the player in the role of a warrior, mage, or rogue coming from an elven, human, or dwarven background. The player character is recruited into the Grey Wardens, an ancient order that stands against monstrous forces known as "Darkspawn", and is tasked with defeating the Archdemon that commands them and ending their invasion. The game is played from a third-person perspective that can be shifted to a top-down perspective. Throughout the game, players encounter various companions, who play major roles in the game's plot and gameplay.

cards.heading: Building a dark fantasy
cards.text: BioWare described Dragon Age: Origins as a "dark heroic fantasy" set in a unique world, and a spiritual successor to their previous Baldur's Gate and Neverwinter Nights franchises. Development of the game began in 2002 and BioWare employed more than 144 voice-actors, and hired Inon Zur to compose the game's music.  While BioWare decided early that it will be a fantasy game, dragons were added late in the game's development after the team used a name generator to create the game's title. The development of the game's console versions was outsourced to Edge of Reality. Origins was released for Microsoft Windows, Xbox 360, and PlayStation 3 in November 2009, and for Mac OS X in December 2009.

cards.heading: Reception and Awakening
cards.text: Origins received critical acclaim upon release, with praise mostly directed at its story, setting, characters, music and combat system. It sold more than 3.2 million copies and 1 million pieces of downloadable content. It won multiple year-end accolades including Game of the Year and Best Role-playing awards from several gaming publications, and has widely been considered to be one of the greatest video games ever made. BioWare released several instances of downloadable content after the game's initial launch, an expansion pack for the game titled Awakening in March 2010, and three sequels, Dragon Age II, Dragon Age: Inquisition, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard, were released in 2011, 2014 and 2024 respectively.

main.title: Band Hero
main.subtitle: The living room becomes a pop stage
main.summary: A pop-oriented sibling to Guitar Hero 5 opens the band format to familiar radio hits and flexible instrument combinations.

cards.heading: A different setlist, familiar freedom
cards.text: Band Hero shifts the emphasis from guitar-led rock towards a broader pop repertoire. The console versions offer sixty-five songs and adopt Guitar Hero 5’s flexible band format: players can join a performance, change difficulty and combine instruments freely. Taylor Swift, Adam Levine and No Doubt appear as performers. The PlayStation 2 version uses the older World Tour engine, so the newer consoles’ features should not be assumed to be identical on every platform.

cards.heading: Assembling the pop band
cards.text: The flexible band format lets players join a performance, change difficulty and combine instrumental roles. Character appearances by Taylor Swift, Adam Levine and No Doubt connect the pop repertoire to recognisable performers. The PlayStation 2 edition uses the older World Tour engine, so the feature set differs from the newer console versions.

main.title: Lego Rock Band
main.subtitle: Build a band and rock the universe
main.summary: Plastic instruments meet minifigures in a musical adventure that turns successful performances into bricks, vehicles and improbable gigs.

cards.heading: A band built from bricks
cards.text: Lego Rock Band joins the four-player instrument performances of Rock Band to LEGO’s customisable minifigures and comic storytelling. Guitar, bass, drums and vocals still follow their own musical parts, but the tour can carry the band from ordinary gigs into fantastical situations. Successful playing earns studs, which help furnish a rock den and develop the band’s identity. Rock Power Challenges make the performance itself the answer to a spectacular problem, such as bringing down a building.

cards.heading: A gentler way onto the stage
cards.text: The console repertoire contains forty-five songs selected for a family audience. A Super Easy setting and other accessibility options help newcomers participate without mastering every note. Supported consoles also offered selected family-appropriate downloadable songs, extending the band's repertoire beyond the disc.

main.title: 3D Dot Game Heroes
main.subtitle: An old adventure with visible depth
main.summary: 3D Dot Game Heroes is Silicon Studio's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 5 November 2009. The kingdom of Dotnia faces a returning evil, sending a hero through fields and dungeons in search of the means to stop it. The structure recalls early console adventures, but the landscape and characters are built from small three-dimensional blocks. Those visible cubes make an old visual language into a physical-looking world. Monsters scatter into pieces, while water and lighting give the deliberately simple shapes an unexpectedly elaborate presentation.

cards.heading: An old adventure with visible depth
cards.text: 3D Dot Game Heroes is Silicon Studio's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 5 November 2009. The kingdom of Dotnia faces a returning evil, sending a hero through fields and dungeons in search of the means to stop it. The structure recalls early console adventures, but the landscape and characters are built from small three-dimensional blocks. Those visible cubes make an old visual language into a physical-looking world. Monsters scatter into pieces, while water and lighting give the deliberately simple shapes an unexpectedly elaborate presentation.

cards.heading: A sword larger than its owner
cards.text: When the hero's health is full, swinging the sword produces a blade of extraordinary size. Keeping that advantage changes the value of avoiding even a small hit. Sword improvements can extend its length and width, letting the player shape how much of a room one attack can reach. Other equipment includes familiar adventure tools such as a boomerang, bow and lantern. Progress comes from exploring the map, finding objects and using them to solve the obstacles inside a dungeon before facing its main threat.

cards.heading: Build the person who enters the dungeon
cards.text: A character editor lets the player assemble a hero from the same blocks that define the world. It can produce a conventional adventurer or a more unlikely figure, making the nostalgic journey visibly personal. References and jokes acknowledge the games whose structure it borrows, while the block-based presentation supplies its own identity. FromSoftware published the original Japanese release, with Atlus and SouthPeak handling later regions. Reviewers generally welcomed its affectionate approach to early action adventures and the contrast between familiar rules and the more modern treatment of their shapes.
